title: Traffic Conductor: Runbook and Ops Templates (wip)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc collects operational templates, ceremony scripts, and a lightweight signal taxonomy for cross-functional staged activation. We use the Traffic Conductor metaphor: a single point (human + dashboard + automations) that coordinates traffic slices, safety checks, and stakeholder comms during progressive exposure of LLM features.

Intended audience:
- Release leads / product owners
- Experiment owners / data scientists running ABs
- Oncall SREs and Platform engineers
- Solutions / customer engineering for safe enterprise rollouts

Core principles (short):
- Minimize blast radius: small slices, short windows, strong gating signals.
- Observable gates: real-time telemetry + simple pass/fail heuristics.
- Single conductor: one owner orchestrates cutover, escalation, and rollback.
- Communication first: short cadence updates and canned messages reduce confusion.

Roles and responsibilities (cheat sheet):
- Traffic Conductor (owner): runs the ceremony, triggers slices, owns decision.
- Signal Steward: defines metrics and thresholds for this activation.
- SRE Oncall: has the revert playbook and permissions to cut traffic.
- Product PM: validates user/metric impact, approves progression.
- Support Liaison: prepped with canned KB and escalation path.

Run cadence (example for 48-hour microactivation):
1) 09:00 - Conductor kickoff (15m): confirm service health, capacity, people oncall.
2) 09:20 - Activate slice A (0.5-1% traffic) + synthetic probe run.
3) 09:35 - Pause and observe (30-60m): watch latency, error rate, quality proxies.
4) 10:35 - Decision point: progress to slice B or revert.
5) Repeat until target exposure reached or incident triggers rollback.

Signal taxonomy (practical & minimal):
- Safety signals (hard stop): error-rate > 3x baseline, user-visible failure surge, PII leakage alarm.
- Latency signals (soft/hard): 95th latency > SLO*1.5 (soft), >SLO*2 (hard).
- Quality signals (experiment-specific): automated eval delta >= predefined threshold OR negative NPS/sentiment on sampled reviews.
- Cost/throughput: token-per-request spike > 2x expected for 10+ minutes -> investigate.
- Behavioral drift: new hallucination class detected by QA sampler -> pause.

Guard thresholds (template):
- Tier 1 (canary gate): must pass all safety signals + latency under soft threshold for 60m.
- Tier 2 (ramp gate): controlled growth only if quality delta within tolerance and cost within budget.
- Escalation: any hard-stop -> immediate revert + incident channel ping.

Operational templates (copy-edit as needed):
- Kickoff checklist: quick health dashboard links (service pods, qps, token queue), contact list, runbook links, rollback command snippets.
- Activation message (to #release channel): short lines: slice %, run id, conductor, expected duration, known caveats.
- Progress update template: minute, slice, primary metric, secondary metric, decision.
- Reversion message: who reverted, timestamp, reason, next steps, postmortem owner.

Decision rubric (simple scoring):
- Score signals as green/amber/red. Green = go, amber = continue only with reduced exposure + extra monitoring, red = revert.
- Use majority-veto: if any hard safety red -> revert.

A/B testing notes (hybrid with conductor):
- Prefer deterministic routing for small cohorts (user-id hash) to prevent contamination.
- Always reserve a clean control slice for at least 2x the canary lifetime to catch slow signals.
- Precompute minimum detectable effect (MDE) for primary metric before ramping beyond pilot. If MDE > expected effect, keep as exploratory and do not auto-ramp.

Oncall and permissions (ops constraints):
- Revert ops must be executable by SRE oncall without product approval during hard-stop windows.
- Conductor must have read-only dashboard links + escalation buttons (Slack or PagerDuty) to reduce manual steps.

Communication artifacts (examples):
- Short public blurb for customers: one-liner, impact, expected behavior, who to contact.
- Internal post-activation note: quick timeline, metrics snapshot, decisions, outstanding follow-ups.

Mini runbook: quick revert steps (example):
1) Identify run_id and slice id on Console.
2) Execute revert API: POST /routing/override {slice:false} (sample command).
3) Confirm traffic shifted, monitor for 15m.
4) Notify stakeholders and open incident if failure persists.

Experiment hygiene / data collection checklist:
- Ensure deterministic membership and no double-exposure across features.
- Attach eval prompt set for quality regression monitoring.
- Store raw samples for manual QA for at least 7 days.

Templates included (at end of doc):
- Slack kickoff message (short)
- Slack progress update (table-like bullet)
- Customer-facing incident blurb
- Post-activation retro prompt for PM + SRE

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Add a small-run synthetic load script tied to canary slice to stress KV cache effects.
- Formalize logger hooks to flag hallucination classes automatically.
- Flesh out MDE calculators per product metric and publish a small spreadsheet for quick reference.

References / links to internal assets (placeholder):
- experiment-templates (confluence)
- rollout-telemetry-dashboards (Grafana folder)
- incident-templates (docs repo)

Quick glossary:
- Conductor: person+dashboard running the activation (not necessarily a PM).
- Slice: traffic partition (percent or cohort).
- Hard-stop: immediate rollback condition.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight — goal is to reduce ceremony friction while preserving safety.
- Feedback wanted: additional MUST signals, preferred comms cadence, and any org-specific permission blockers.

Scratch area (raw ideas):
- Consider a "dry-run" mode that simulates gate thresholds with historical traffic to tune thresholds before live activation.
- Explore a small runbook widget in Console to auto-fill messages and generate run_ids.

— end —
